name: windows-appinit-hook-registry
description: Enables the two global user-mode DLL-load hooks: sets LoadAppInit_DLLs=1 plus AppInit_DLLs pointing at a staged library (DLL_PATH, default C:\Windows\System32\inproc_helper.dll), and registers the same path as an AppCertDLLs value under Session Manager. In a real intrusion this is how a hide-library gets into every GUI/user32 process and into every process that calls CreateProcess — the catalog's only comparable detection advice is that a populated value is itself the tell. A hook target must be a real PE: a non-PE or dangling value breaks 32-bit process startup (Bad Image 0xc000012f) and stalls the first-logon setup, so the plant only writes a payload when DLL_PAYLOAD_B64 is supplied. Without a payload it removes the stale file and leaves no hook registered at all, so first-logon is never blocked; with a payload, the misconfiguration (persistent machine-wide hook registration) is the finding. Realistic cover: some legit endpoint agents historically used AppInit_DLLs, so the key existing is normal — the unexpected value is not. Defender notice: check HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows and ...\Control\Session Manager\AppCertDLLs. Derived from C3rberus windows_hide_library; XOR config blob and hooking code dropped, load mechanism kept. Difficulty: 4 (ultra).
